name: unifi-mcp
description: Monitor and manage your Ubiquiti UniFi Network: sites, devices, clients, WiFi, firewall and more.
long_description:
An open-source MCP server for Ubiquiti **UniFi Network**. Ask about your network in plain English: health checks, weak WiFi clients, firmware updates, firewall and port-forward reviews. If you allow it, Claude can also make changes.

- **Read-only by default.** Changes need *Allow changes*, and deleting configuration needs *Allow deletes* as well. Destructive tools are labelled so Claude asks before running them, and passwords and keys are redacted from output.
- **Works with your controller.** UniFi OS consoles (UDM, UCG, UDR, UX, Cloud Key Gen2+, UniFi OS Server) and legacy self-hosted Network applications (up to Network 10.6), with an API key or a local account.
- **Pin the certificate.** Consoles use a self-signed certificate: set the *TLS certificate fingerprint* so nobody on the network can impersonate the controller.

unifi-mcp is an independent community project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Ubiquiti Inc.

tools.name: unifi_check_firewall_path
tools.description: Read-only "what if": for a new connection from source to destination (and destination port), work out the source and destination zones from the networks' subnets (addresses outside every local subnet are in the External zone), then walk the enabled zone-based firewall policies between those zones in index order and report the first that matches, so the verdict (ALLOW, BLOCK or REJECT). Policies that might match first but can't be evaluated from addresses (apps, domains, regions, IP or port groups, schedules) are listed under may_match_first, and when one of them is listed the verdict is only certain if it doesn't match. Traffic rules that match the source and destination are listed too. It reads the configuration only: no traffic is sent, and the controller's own evaluation can differ in details. Network 9.0+ (zone-based firewall).

tools.name: unifi_check_updates
tools.description: Check for updates in one call: the latest Network application version the controller knows of (controller), the devices with a firmware upgrade (current and available version) and how many are up to date. For every device's firmware use unifi_get_firmware_status.

tools.name: unifi_get_client
tools.description: Get one client by MAC: its stored settings (alias, note, fixed IP, blocked) merged with live connection details when it is connected, and an online flag. Errors if the controller has never seen the MAC.

tools.name: unifi_get_dashboard
tools.description: Get the aggregated dashboard the UniFi UI shows: WAN/ISP quality history (latency, packet loss, availability, throughput), WiFi experience and client mix. v2 API, Network 7.4+; large response.

tools.name: unifi_get_device
tools.description: Get one device by MAC: its list summary plus serial, ports, radio settings and stats, outlets, WAN links, system stats, load average, PoE use and LED settings. Errors if no device has that MAC. For a switch's ports with LLDP neighbours and profile names use unifi_list_switch_ports.

tools.name: unifi_get_dpi_stats
tools.description: Get deep packet inspection (traffic identification) statistics, by application or by category, biggest first: site-wide, or per client when macs are given. Uses the v2 traffic endpoint (Network 9+), with names from the official API when an API key is configured, and falls back to the classic stat/sitedpi on older versions. Requires traffic identification to be enabled.

tools.name: unifi_get_firewall_policy_ordering
tools.description: Get the evaluation order of user-defined policies between a source and destination zone (beforeSystemDefined / afterSystemDefined policy ID lists). Uses the official integration API, so it requires API-key authentication (UNIFI_API_KEY) and Network 9.0+.

tools.name: unifi_get_firmware_status
tools.description: List each device's model and firmware version, whether an upgrade is available (and to which version) or running, with the number of upgradable devices; include_available adds the firmware images the controller can install. Availability is as of the controller's last check with Ubiquiti. unifi_check_updates also covers Network application updates.

tools.name: unifi_get_guest_portal_settings
tools.description: Get guest portal / hotspot settings: authentication method, session length, voucher/password/payment options, redirect, allowed subnets.

tools.name: unifi_get_rf_scan
tools.description: Get an access point's last RF/spectrum scan: whether a scan is running, when it last ran, and utilization and interference per channel. Returns scanning: false and no results if the AP has no scan.

tools.name: unifi_get_security_settings
tools.description: Get threat management (IDS/IPS mode, categories, protected networks), traffic identification (DPI) and country/region blocking (geo-IP) settings. Optionally list the IPS categories the controller supports (Network 8+).

tools.name: unifi_get_site_health
tools.description: Get a site's status per subsystem (wan, lan, wlan, vpn, www): status, ISP, WAN IP, latency, throughput, and device and client counts. The quickest overall check of a site. For WAN quality over time use unifi_get_dashboard.

tools.name: unifi_get_site_settings
tools.description: Get site-wide settings. Each setting is an object identified by `key`, e.g. mgmt (auto-upgrade, LEDs, SSH), country, locale, ntp, snmp, mdns (multicast DNS), rsyslogd (remote syslog), connectivity, guest_access, ips, dpi, usg (gateway: DNS, geo-IP, UPnP...), radius, network_optimization, super_mgmt (controller-wide, including auto-backup). Omit `key` to list all keys.

tools.name: unifi_get_speedtest_results
tools.description: List the gateway's WAN speed test results, newest first (default last 168 hours): time, download and upload in Mbps, latency in ms and test server.

tools.name: unifi_get_system_info
tools.description: Get the controller's own details (stat/sysinfo): Network application version, hostname, timezone, uptime and whether an application update is available. To check application and device firmware updates together use unifi_check_updates. For each device's firmware use unifi_get_firmware_status.

tools.name: unifi_get_system_log
tools.description: Read one class of the v2 system log (Network 8+), paged (default 50 entries from the last 168 hours): device-alert (default), client-alert, admin-activity (logins and config changes), update-alert, threat-alert (IPS/honeypot), vpn-alert, triggers (traffic/firewall rule hits) or next-ai-alert. Entries have time, key, category, severity, title, message, device and client. unifi_list_events reads the classic event log.

tools.name: unifi_get_traffic_report
tools.description: Get historical time-series statistics in buckets of 5 minutes to a month. scope=site for whole-site traffic and client counts, gw for gateway CPU/memory/WAN traffic, ap for per-AP traffic, user for per-client traffic (pass macs). For traffic by application use unifi_get_dpi_stats.

tools.name: unifi_list_acl_rules
tools.description: List switch ACL rules (MAC ACLs that allow or block traffic between devices inside one network, enforced by UniFi switches). Rules are processed in acl_index order. Needs Network 9.4+.

tools.name: unifi_list_admins
tools.description: List a site's administrator accounts, or every site's with all_sites: true: name, email, role, super admin and owner flags, permissions, sites and last login.

tools.name: unifi_list_alarms
tools.description: List controller alarms (alerts), newest first, with time, key, subsystem and message; archived alarms are left out unless include_archived. On Network 10.6+, where the classic alarm list is gone, returns the v2 system log's entries of min_severity (default high) from the last hours (default 168) instead. For the full event history use unifi_list_events.

tools.name: unifi_list_anomalies
tools.description: List anomalies the controller detected per client or device (e.g. high latency, DNS timeouts, poor WiFi experience), default last 24 hours. Rows are returned as the controller reports them; not available on every Network version.

tools.name: unifi_list_ap_groups
tools.description: List access point groups (id, name, member AP MACs, device count, default flag), which choose the APs that broadcast each WiFi network. Network 7.x+ (v2 API).

tools.name: unifi_list_backups
tools.description: List the backups stored on the controller, newest first: filename, time, Network version, size in MB and type.

tools.name: unifi_list_bandwidth_profiles
tools.description: List bandwidth profiles (user groups): per-client download and upload caps in kbps ("unlimited" when uncapped) that WiFi networks and clients can be assigned.

tools.name: unifi_list_client_sessions
tools.description: List client connection sessions, newest first (default last 168 hours): client, IP, connect and disconnect times, duration, AP, SSID, network and bytes; filter by client MAC or guest/user. For who is connected now use unifi_list_clients.

tools.name: unifi_list_clients
tools.description: List the clients connected now, with IP, network, AP or switch port, signal, rates, usage and uptime; filter by connection type, guests, network or AP. For offline clients and stored settings (alias, fixed IP, blocked) use unifi_list_known_clients. For connection history use unifi_list_client_sessions.

tools.name: unifi_list_content_filters
tools.description: List content filtering profiles (blocked categories, safe search, target networks/clients). v2 API, Network 8.1+.

tools.name: unifi_list_devices
tools.description: List the site's UniFi devices (gateways, switches, access points...) with state, model, firmware, IP, uptime, CPU and memory load and client counts; filter by type or state. For one device's ports, radios and uplink use unifi_get_device.

tools.name: unifi_list_dns_records
tools.description: List the gateway's local DNS records (A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT, SRV, NS) with name, value, TTL and enabled state. Network 8.2+ (v2 static-dns). For a public hostname that follows the WAN IP use unifi_list_dynamic_dns.

tools.name: unifi_list_dynamic_dns
tools.description: List the gateway's dynamic DNS entries, which keep a public hostname pointed at the WAN IP: provider service, hostname, login, server and WAN interface (passwords redacted).

tools.name: unifi_list_events
tools.description: List recent controller events, newest first (default last 24 hours): client connects and roams, device restarts, upgrades and the like, with time, key, subsystem and message. Falls back to the v2 system log's device and client alerts where the classic event log is gone or empty. For other log classes (admin activity, threats, VPN...) use unifi_get_system_log; for unresolved problems use unifi_list_alarms.

tools.name: unifi_list_firewall_groups
tools.description: List firewall groups (address groups, IPv6 address groups and port groups) referenced by firewall rules and policies.

tools.name: unifi_list_firewall_policies
tools.description: List zone-based firewall policies (Network 9.0+) sorted by index: action, source and destination (zone and match), protocol, connection states, schedule and logging. Predefined (system) policies are left out unless include_predefined. On classic firewalls use unifi_list_firewall_rules; to find the policy that applies to a connection use unifi_check_firewall_path.

tools.name: unifi_list_firewall_rules
tools.description: List classic firewall rules, sorted by ruleset (WAN_IN, LAN_IN, ...) and rule_index, with action, protocol, source and destination. Not available on Network 11+ or on sites migrated to the zone-based firewall (Network 9+): use unifi_list_firewall_policies there.

tools.name: unifi_list_firewall_zones
tools.description: List zone-based firewall zones (Network 9.0+) with zone_key, system-defined flag, network IDs and integration_id. Firewall policies and unifi_check_firewall_path refer to zones by these IDs.

tools.name: unifi_list_guest_authorizations
tools.description: List guest portal/hotspot authorizations, newest first (default last 168 hours): client MAC and IP, method, voucher code, start and end, bytes and expired flag.

tools.name: unifi_list_hotspot_operators
tools.description: List hotspot operator accounts (staff who can log in to the hotspot manager to issue vouchers).

tools.name: unifi_list_known_clients
tools.description: List every client the controller has stored, online or offline, most recently seen first, with alias, note, fixed IP and block status. For live connection details use unifi_list_clients or unifi_get_client.

tools.name: unifi_list_nat_rules
tools.description: List NAT rules (DNAT, SNAT and masquerade, the predefined ones included) with type, interfaces, translated IP and port, source and destination. Needs Network 9.0+ with a UniFi gateway and the zone-based firewall. Simple port forwards are separate: unifi_list_port_forwards.

tools.name: unifi_list_networks
tools.description: List every configured network (LANs/VLANs, WANs and VPNs) with purpose, subnet, VLAN, DHCP range, domain and firewall zone. For WAN connection settings and health use unifi_list_wans. For VPN settings use unifi_list_vpns.

tools.name: unifi_list_oon_policies
tools.description: List object-oriented networking (OON) policies: rules attached to clients or client groups that schedule or block internet access and apps (secure), limit bandwidth (qos) or route through a VPN (route). Needs Network 9.4+ with a UniFi gateway.

tools.name: unifi_list_port_forwards
tools.description: List port forwards (WAN port to internal IP and port) with protocol, WAN interface, allowed source and logging. Custom DNAT/SNAT rules are in unifi_list_nat_rules, and the rules that filter traffic in unifi_list_firewall_policies (unifi_list_firewall_rules on classic firewalls).

tools.name: unifi_list_port_profiles
tools.description: List switch port profiles (reusable port configurations): forwarding mode, native and tagged networks, PoE, speed, isolation, storm control and port security. unifi_list_switch_ports shows which profile each port uses.

tools.name: unifi_list_qos_rules
tools.description: List QoS rules from the policy table (recent Network 9.x/10.x with a UniFi gateway): objective (LIMIT, PRIORITIZE or LIMIT_AND_PRIORITIZE), rate limits in kbps, the clients/networks they apply to and the apps, IPs, regions or domains they match.

tools.name: unifi_list_radius_accounts
tools.description: List users of the built-in RADIUS server (used for L2TP VPN and WPA-Enterprise). Passwords redacted.

tools.name: unifi_list_radius_profiles
tools.description: List RADIUS profiles used by WPA-Enterprise WiFi, 802.1X switch ports and L2TP VPN (secrets redacted).

tools.name: unifi_list_rogue_aps
tools.description: List access points your APs can hear (neighbours and ones flagged as rogue), strongest first (default seen in the last 24 hours): SSID, BSSID, channel, band, signal, security, vendor, which of your APs saw it and when. For per-channel interference use unifi_get_rf_scan.

tools.name: unifi_list_routes
tools.description: List user-defined static routes: destination CIDR, type (nexthop, interface or blackhole), next hop or interface, distance and enabled. With active: true, return the gateway's live routing table instead, system routes included (stat/routing; not on every version). To send chosen clients or destinations out a particular WAN or VPN use unifi_list_traffic_routes.

tools.name: unifi_list_sites
tools.description: List the controller's sites with id, name, description, role and device_count. Pass a site's `name` (not its description) as the `site` argument of other tools.

tools.name: unifi_list_switch_ports
tools.description: List a switch's ports with link state, speed, PoE, assigned profile, LLDP neighbours (what is plugged in: chassis ID, description and remote port), link aggregation and any per-port overrides configured on the device.

tools.name: unifi_list_threats
tools.description: List IDS/IPS threat events detected by the gateway, newest first (default last 24 hours): signature, category, severity, action taken, protocol, and source and destination IP, port and country.

tools.name: unifi_list_traffic_flows
tools.description: List recent traffic flows seen by the gateway (Insights > Flows): source and destination client, IP, domain and network, app/service, allowed or blocked, risk, bytes and the policies that matched. This is an expensive query on the gateway, so it looks back 15 minutes (hours: 0.25) and returns 50 flows per page by default; narrow it with client_mac, action, risk or search (applied by the controller to app, domain, client name and more) before widening the window. Recent Network 9.x/10.x with a UniFi gateway.

tools.name: unifi_list_traffic_routes
tools.description: List traffic routes (policy-based routing): which clients or networks, and which destinations (domains, IPs, regions or all internet), are sent out a given WAN or VPN client network, with kill switch and next hop. Plain destination-based static routes are in unifi_list_routes.

tools.name: unifi_list_traffic_rules
tools.description: List traffic rules (v2 API) that block, allow or rate-limit traffic from clients or networks by app, app category, domain, IP, region or all internet, with schedule and bandwidth limit. Zone-based firewall policies are separate (unifi_list_firewall_policies).

tools.name: unifi_list_vouchers
tools.description: List hotspot vouchers with code, note, duration, quota and times used, status, rate and data limits, and creation time. For who redeemed them use unifi_list_guest_authorizations.

tools.name: unifi_list_vpns
tools.description: List the gateway's VPN servers (WireGuard, OpenVPN, L2TP), VPN clients and site-to-site VPNs with kind, enabled state, subnet, port, WAN interface, peer and remote subnets and DNS. raw: true shows every field.

tools.name: unifi_list_wans
tools.description: List WAN connections with connection type, VLAN, static IP or PPPoE user, DNS, failover and load balancing, Smart Queues and ISP speeds, plus live WAN health (status, WAN IP, ISP, uptime).

tools.name: unifi_list_wlans
tools.description: List WiFi networks (SSIDs) with security and WPA mode, bands, linked network, AP groups, bandwidth and RADIUS profiles, guest and hidden flags, client isolation, MAC filter and enabled state (passphrases redacted).

prompts.name: network_health_check
prompts.description: Overall health review of a UniFi site: WAN, devices, clients, alarms and recent problems.
prompts.text:
Do a health check of my UniFi network.
1. unifi_get_site_health: status of WAN/LAN/WLAN/VPN, ISP, latency, throughput.
2. unifi_list_devices: anything not "connected", high CPU/memory, firmware upgrades available, recent reboots (short uptime).
3. unifi_list_alarms and unifi_list_events (last 24h): recurring or serious issues.
4. unifi_list_clients (connection: wireless): clients with weak signal (below -70 dBm) or low satisfaction.
5. unifi_get_speedtest_results if available.
Report: a one-line verdict, then problems ordered by severity, each with evidence and a suggested fix. Keep healthy areas to one line each. Don't change anything.

prompts.name: troubleshoot_client
prompts.description: Investigate why a specific client (by MAC, name or IP) has connectivity problems.
prompts.text:
Troubleshoot connectivity for the client "${arguments.client}" on my UniFi network.
1. Find it: unifi_list_clients (search) if online, otherwise unifi_list_known_clients; then unifi_get_client by MAC.
2. Check: online state, IP and network/VLAN, fixed IP, blocked/guest status, signal/satisfaction/rates (wireless) or switch port (wired).
3. The AP or switch it uses: unifi_get_device (port errors/speed, radio channel utilisation, uptime).
4. History: unifi_list_client_sessions for this MAC (frequent reconnects?), unifi_list_events.
5. If relevant: unifi_list_firewall_rules / unifi_list_traffic_rules / unifi_list_qos_rules / unifi_list_oon_policies / unifi_list_content_filters for rules affecting it, and unifi_list_traffic_flows (client_mac, action: blocked) for traffic being blocked.
Report the most likely cause(s) with evidence and concrete next steps. Ask before making any change.

prompts.name: security_review
prompts.description: Review the site's security posture: threat management, firewall, port forwards, WiFi security and admins.
prompts.text:
Review the security of my UniFi network.
Check:
- unifi_get_security_settings: is IDS/IPS on, in which mode, on which networks; country blocking.
- unifi_list_threats (last 7 days, hours: 168): notable signatures, repeat offenders, internal hosts involved.
- unifi_list_port_forwards: exposed services, forwards open to any source.
- unifi_list_firewall_rules and unifi_list_firewall_policies: overly broad allow rules, missing inter-VLAN isolation.
- unifi_list_nat_rules: DNAT rules that expose internal hosts; unifi_list_acl_rules: switch-level isolation inside networks.
- unifi_list_wlans: open or WPA2-only networks where WPA3 is possible, guest networks without isolation.
- unifi_list_networks: guest/IoT segmentation.
- unifi_list_admins: number of admins and roles.
- unifi_get_system_log (class: admin-activity): recent logins and changes.
Report findings as High / Medium / Low with the reason and a specific remediation. Don't change anything.

prompts.name: firmware_review
prompts.description: List devices and the controller with available updates and propose a safe upgrade order.
prompts.text:
Review firmware on my UniFi network.
1. unifi_check_updates: controller version and devices with upgrades.
2. unifi_list_devices: model, current firmware, uptime and client count for each device needing an update.
Propose an upgrade plan that minimises disruption: access points first (one at a time where they overlap), then switches from the edge inwards, gateway last; note which upgrades will drop clients. Don't start any upgrade unless I confirm.

prompts.name: wifi_optimization
prompts.description: Analyse WiFi channels, utilisation, interference and client experience and suggest improvements.
prompts.text:
Analyse and suggest improvements for the WiFi on my UniFi network.
1. unifi_list_devices (type: access_point), then unifi_get_device for each AP: channel, width, transmit power, channel utilisation, satisfaction, client count per radio.
2. unifi_list_rogue_aps: strongest neighbouring networks per channel.
3. unifi_list_clients (connection: wireless): weak-signal and low-rate clients, clients stuck on 2.4 GHz.
4. unifi_list_wlans: number of SSIDs, bands, minimum data rates.
Recommend specific changes (channel plan, widths, power levels, SSID consolidation, band steering) with the reason for each, ordered by expected impact. Don't apply changes unless I confirm.

url.title: Controller URL
url.description: Address of your UniFi console, e.g. https://192.168.1.1. For a legacy self-hosted Network application, include the port, e.g. https://192.168.1.10:8443.

api_key.title: API key
api_key.description: Recommended on UniFi OS consoles. Create one in UniFi Network → Settings → Control Plane → Integrations. Leave empty to use a username and password instead.

username.title: Username
username.description: A local (not Ubiquiti cloud) account, used instead of an API key. Required for legacy controllers.

password.title: Password
password.description: The local account's password, used with the username.

tls_fingerprint.title: TLS certificate fingerprint
tls_fingerprint.description: Recommended for an https controller with a self-signed certificate: its SHA-256 fingerprint (AA:BB:…), so nobody on the network can impersonate it. See the security docs for how to get it.

verify_ssl.title: Verify certificate (true/false)
verify_ssl.description: Leave empty when you set a fingerprint or CA file. true: the controller has a publicly trusted certificate. false: skip the check (insecure: anyone on the network path could capture your credentials).

ca_file.title: CA certificate file
ca_file.description: Optional PEM file with the CA that signed the controller's certificate, instead of a fingerprint.

site.title: Site
site.description: The site's short name (from the URL, e.g. default), used when a request doesn't name a site.

allow_writes.title: Allow changes
allow_writes.description: Let Claude change your network: restart devices, block clients, edit WiFi, firewall and networks. Off means read-only.

allow_deletes.title: Allow deletes
allow_deletes.description: Also let Claude delete configuration and forget clients. Needs Allow changes.

allow_secrets.title: Allow secrets
allow_secrets.description: Let Claude ask for unredacted passwords and keys (include_secrets) and use the WiFi QR tool. Off keeps all output redacted.

toolsets.title: Toolsets
toolsets.description: Optional comma-separated list to expose fewer tools, e.g. overview,devices,clients,wifi,monitoring. Empty means all except raw, which has to be listed by name.

raw_allowed_paths.title: Raw API paths
raw_allowed_paths.description: Optional comma-separated API path prefixes, e.g. /api/s/default/stat, that limit the raw API tool (toolset raw) to those paths. Empty allows any path.

audit_log.title: Audit log file
audit_log.description: Optional full path to a file, e.g. /Users/you/unifi-mcp-audit.jsonl, where every change Claude makes or previews is appended as a JSON line. The file is created if it doesn't exist; its folder must exist. stderr writes the lines to Claude Desktop's MCP log instead. Off when left empty.

backup_dir.title: Backup folder
backup_dir.description: Optional folder where Claude can save controller backups (unifi_download_backup, needs Allow changes). Backups contain the whole configuration, including passwords. Off when left empty.
